Thanks — I’ll loop in the security team now.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Security Team <security@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Discovery follow-up: security/compliance & pen-test info

Marissa —

Attached are the two redacted artifacts we typically share with prospective customers:
- Redwood_PenTest_Report_2025.pdf (external pentest summary, redacted findings, high-level remediation status)
- SOC2_Type2_Report_2025.pdf (redacted SOC 2 Type II report, covers infrastructure & platform controls)

Vulnerability management summary (short):
- Regular scanning:
  - Internal automated scans: weekly (SAST/DAST + dependency scanning).
  - External vulnerability scans: weekly network scans and monthly authenticated scans where applicable.
  - Third-party external penetration test: annually, plus ad-hoc engagements for major releases.
- Triage & SLAs:
  - Critical (CVSS 9-10 / active exploit): initial response within 24 hours; patch/mitigation timeline agreed per incident (usually 72 hours for public-facing infra).
  - High/P1 (CVSS 7-8.9): initial response within 72 hours; remediation tracked in our tracker with SLA depending on risk and customer impact.
  - Medium/Low: prioritized by risk and planned into next sprint cycles.
- Remediation verification: fixes validated by targeted re-scans and, in high-risk cases, re-test by our external tester.
- Disclosure/PSIRT policy: We follow a coordinated disclosure process — notify affected customers, provide remediation guidance, and publish security advisories for widely affecting issues. We redact customer-identifying details in external reports.

If they want us to fill the questionnaire, we can return a filled PDF (we typically provide redacted docs + answers in their template). I’ll copy the actual attachments for your outbound.

Attachment: Redwood_PenTest_Report_2025.pdf (PDF, 2.3MB)
Attachment: SOC2_Type2_Report_2025.pdf (PDF, 1.8MB)

Let me know if you want any additional contractor statements or MSK/KMS diagrams for HIPAA flows.

Thanks,
Rishi
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
